preamble: Change of the voiced dental fricative [ð] to the alveolar tap [ɾ]. In Finnish, the Old Literary Finnish weak-grade fricative [ð] (spelled d or dh) was lost from most dialects; in South Ostrobothnian and other western dialects it became a tapped or trilled r, so standard tahdon 'I want' and uuden 'new (gen.)' correspond to dialectal taharon and uuren.

examples.note: Word-internally r stands where the standard language has d (the spelling-pronunciation reflex of old ð).
From the dialect sentence 'Mä taharon uuren puukoon lahajaks' ('I want a new knife as a present').

sources: Mustanoja, L., & O'Dell, M. (2007). Suomen d ja r sosiofoneettisessa kentässä. Virittäjä, 111(1), 56. https://journal.fi/virittaja/article/view/40542
